chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Pilgrimage (Hajj) and Minor Pilgrimage ('Umrah) remove poverty and sins, just as the bellows (khir) removes the dross of iron."

Muawiya said: "I asked him: Which is superior, one Hajj or the freeing of a slave? He said: 'One Hajj is superior.' I said: 'And two (Hajjs)?' He said: 'One Hajj is superior.' Muawiya said: 'So I kept increasing (the number of slaves) and he kept saying: "One Hajj is superior," until I reached thirty slaves, and he said: "One Hajj is superior."'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of Hajj compared to freeing a slave?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on the rewards of Hajj, this hadith utilizes the metaphor of the blacksmith’s hammer (al-keer) purging iron impurities to illustrate how Hajj and 'Umrah cleanse both spiritual sins and material poverty. The Imam’s repeated affirmation that a single Hajj surpasses the emancipation of thirty slaves underscores the unique, comprehensive merit of the pilgrimage in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from other major acts of worship like manumission.
